Let \(V\) be the vector space with basis \(e_S\), \(S\subseteq[10]\). Define
\[
Ue_S=\sum_{i\notin S}e_{S\cup\{i\}},\qquad De_S=\sum_{i\in S}e_{S\setminus\{i\}}.
\]
Then the off-diagonal part of \(A\) is \(-(U+D)\), while on level \(|S|=k\), the diagonal contribution is
\[
11+k(10-k).
\]

Use the standard Boolean-lattice decomposition into chains. For each \(j=0,\dots,5\), let \(H_j=\ker(D:V_j\to V_{j-1})\). Then
\[
\dim H_j=\binom{10}{j}-\binom{10}{j-1},
\]
and for \(h\in H_j\), the span of
\[
h,\ Uh,\ U^2h,\dots,U^{10-2j}h
\]
is \(A\)-invariant. The identity
\[
DU^m h=m(10-2j-m+1)U^{m-1}h
\]
follows from \([D,U]\) acting on level \(k\) as multiplication by \(10-2k\).

So on the \(j\)-chain, with \(m=0,\dots,N\), \(N=10-2j\), the tridiagonal determinant \(\Delta_j\) satisfies
\[
p_{-1}=1,\qquad p_0=11+j(10-j),
\]
\[
p_m=\bigl(11+(j+m)(10-j-m)\bigr)p_{m-1}
-m(N-m+1)p_{m-2}.
\]
Computing these six recurrences gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
j&\dim H_j&\Delta_j\\ \hline
0&1&1151460143640576\\
1&9&11577094230016\\
2&35&31270855680\\
3&75&44407872\\
4&90&43960\\
5&42&36
\end{array}
\]
Hence
\[
\det A=\prod_{j=0}^5 \Delta_j^{\binom{10}{j}-\binom{10}{j-1}}.
\]

Factoring the result,
\[
\boxed{
2^{1274}3^{419}5^{125}7^{118}11\cdot23\cdot31^{110}\cdot157^{90}\cdot523\cdot829^{75}\cdot1249\cdot1601^9\cdot5147^9\cdot7297^{35}
}.
\]
